nina: Heads-up: our sample app onboarding hit a nasty auth precedence bug. If you set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT, the runtime sometimes swaps your explicit env key for the project's org-default key.

jon: whoa. minimal repro?

nina: repro steps:
1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_user_123
2) export REDWOOD_PROJECT=team-x
3) run `rw sampleapp start`
Logs show: `Using API key from env: pk_user_123` then a split-second later `Switched to org default key: pk_org_default` and requests go to org tenant.

paul: that would totally confuse new users. is the CLI caching something or reading metadata?

nina: traced it. auth/resolvers.ts calls ProjectProvider.resolve() early when REDWOOD_PROJECT is set. ProjectProvider tries metadata, and if project lookup fails it returns org default — but it never asked if an env var or CLI flag was present first.

lee: so the precedence is wrong. expected: CLI flag > env var > config file > project metadata/org default. current: project metadata can override env var.

jon: quick hack: can we short-circuit ProjectProvider to check `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` and `argv['--api-key']` before metadata call?

paul: that's reasonable. also need tests to cover: env var preserved, flag overrides, and a fallback when project metadata provides an explicit project-scoped key.

nina: i'll open a tiny fix PR and add unit/integration tests. I'll also add a note to sampleapp README and onboarding doc to avoid setting both env var and project at the same time until fixed.

ci-bot: nina/fix-auth-precedence opened PR #712 — 3 checks queued

jon: could we add an opt-in verbose debug like `rw auth:debug` so support can see which provider gave the key? would have avoided the customer call.

lee: yes pls. `rw auth:whoami --verbose` would be great for support playbooks.

paul: also consider telemetry event when an override happens so we can detect users getting silently routed to org tenant.

nina: good idea. I'll add a simple audit log entry in the resolver when it falls back to org default. PR will include tests and a changelog entry.

jon: thanks. this will save a lot of onboarding time. keep us posted :raised_hands:
